5 “return” metrics.

None of them mean the same thing.

Join my next free live executive masterclass and learn to pick the right return metric for every decision → https://bit.ly/ceo-mcs-x

Yet most CEOs use them interchangeably in board decks, capital discussions, and investment reviews (and no one pushes back).

That's not a finance problem. It's a decision-making problem.

Because the metric you choose determines the question you're answering.
 
And if you're answering the wrong question with confidence, the analysis isn't protecting you.

It's misleading you.

Here's the lens each one gives you:

ROI - Return on Investment
↳ Did this specific investment pay off?
↳ Simple entry point. Misses leverage, time, and ongoing costs.

ROIC - Return on Invested Capital
↳ How efficiently is the business converting all capital into profit?
↳ The clearest signal of long-term capital discipline.

ROE - Return on Equity
↳ What return are shareholders earning on their equity?
↳ Can be inflated by debt. Never read it without context.

ROCE - Return on Capital Employed
↳ How well is all long-term capital being deployed?
↳ Better than ROE in capital-intensive businesses.

ROA - Return on Assets
↳ Are the assets generating adequate earnings?
↳ Cross-industry comparable. Depreciation makes it tricky in asset-heavy sectors.

The bottom line…

ROI tells you what happened on one bet.
ROIC tells you how well you're running the whole business.

Knowing which question you're actually asking, that's financial intelligence.

♦
